jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Tiny Hypnotist
jokes.joke: I hired a hypnotherapist to get my toddler to sleep. He stood in the nursery swinging a watch, saying, “Your eyelids are getting heavy.” My kid stared at him, unimpressed, then slowly made the hypnotherapist put on pajamas, drink warm milk, and apologize to a stuffed giraffe. That’s when I realized: I didn’t have a bedtime problem. I had middle management.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Under
jokes.joke: I went to a hypnotherapist to fix my anger issues. Guy's got the softest voice in the world, tells me, 'You are calm, you are safe, on the count of three you will feel total peace.' Counts to three, and the second I'm under, HIS phone rings, it's his ex, and he screams 'TELL YOUR LAWYER TO EAT GLASS!' I woke up more furious than when I walked in. Cured me of therapy, not anger.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Heavy Eyelids
jokes.joke: We hired a hypnotherapist to come into the nursery because our toddler absolutely refuses to nap. The guy dims the lights, pulls out a swinging pocket watch, and starts softly chanting, \"Your eyelids are getting heavy...\" Forty minutes later, I walk in to check on them. The hypnotherapist is curled up in the crib snoring, and my kid is on the rug going through his wallet.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Hypno Nursery Shift
jokes.joke: Folks, I took a job as a hypnotherapist at this busy nursery. Parents drop off fussy babies, I swing the watch and whisper 'you're getting very sleepy.' Boom, instant silence. Felt like a genius until I tested it on myself during break. Woke up crammed in a crib, knees by my ears, sucking on a pacifier. The director walks in and goes, 'Great work on the kids... but you're covering the next diaper change.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Nap Time Emergency
jokes.joke: I was helping out at a friend’s nursery, and I didn’t realize toddlers can be… volatile. One kid looked me dead in the eyes, picked up a juice box, and whispered, “Boom.” Then he squeezed it so hard it exploded all over me. I wasn’t even mad—I just saluted him and said, “Sir, your nap time is whenever you say it is.”

scores.comment: Clear premise and a funny reversal, with the therapist becoming the anger trigger. Strong wording, though the final tag is more tidy than explosive.
Best clean comic image in the batch. The toddler going through the wallet is a sharp, visual final turn that lands naturally.
Understandable and on prompt, but it drifts into broad cartoon logic. The crib and diaper-change payoff feels forced rather than surprising.
A solid mild joke with a clear toddler-as-threat angle. The final line gets a smile, but the escalation is familiar and not especially sharp.
Clean reversal with escalating specificity (pajamas, milk, giraffe apology) and a sharp closing line reframing it as workplace hierarchy; strongest tag of the batch.
Same reversal premise but less escalation; wallet-rifling image is amusing but the closer doesn't carry as much punch as it could.
Solid visual (knees by ears, pacifier) but the diaper-duty tag reads as a mundane task assignment rather than a real twist; slightly overlong setup.
Fun escalation from deadpan menace to exploding juice box; the salute line is a decent capper though not a huge laugh.
Excellent craft and strong punchline cleanly linking toddler manipulation to corporate middle management.
Competent execution but heavily relies on the familiar trope of the deeply unstable therapist having an outburst.
A bit cartoonish in its logic; the premise is mildly amusing but the final diaper change line is a weak payoff.
Solid visual escalation with the juice box intimidation, though the final salute reaction feels slightly formulaic.
The toddler making the hypnotherapist apologize to a stuffed giraffe before realizing it's a middle management issue was a sharp role reversal.
The hypnotherapist screaming 'TELL YOUR LAWYER TO EAT GLASS!' at his ex during the session perfectly undercut the calm induction.
The hypnotherapist curled up in the crib snoring while the kid went through his wallet delivered a great visual switcheroo.
The toddler whispering 'Boom' before squeezing the juice box to explode all over everything captured the volatile nursery energy well.
Clean premise and a solid turn; middle‑management tag is funny but not highly surprising.
Strong contrast gag; the therapist’s outburst lands, though the shape is familiar.
Wallet gag is predictable; readable and competent but not especially memorable.
Straightforward escalation; pacifier image works but the turn is expected.
